sources.entry: Charrette by Stefan Teofanovic - A Claude Code plugin with agent skills for designing software before code is written: brainstorm boards, plans cut into slices and run by subagents, working HTML mockups, development workbenches and layered pull request reviews. Every document renders live in a bundled local viewer with Mermaid diagrams, outside the repository.

summary.one_liner: Swarmstorm (formerly Charrette) is a set of MIT-licensed agent skills and plugins for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that run parallel coding agents coordinated on a shared board, with prototypes, plans, QA verifiers and a local viewer.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a plugin for Claude Code, Codex and Cursor that orchestrates several coding agents working in parallel, each in its own worktree, which negotiate shared file locks on a board before merging into one branch. It provides a local viewer (aiview at localhost:4321) that renders plans, boards, clickable HTML prototypes, workbenches, diagrams and reports, with Mermaid diagrams, stored outside the repository in a data home folder. Skills cover planning (write-plan, interview, cold-read), execution (execute-plan, orchestrate-plan), build-verify loops where verifier agents test the running app, brainstorm and debate protocols run by role-playing seats, and layered pull request review (pr-review). It also includes a dependency-graph skill for JavaScript/TypeScript projects using dependency-cruiser, and complexity-rework guidance with cyclomatic and cognitive measures. The README says the plugin ships no hooks and installs no packages at runtime.
use_cases: run several coding agents in parallel on one feature
plan and prototype a UI before coding it
brainstorm or debate a design decision with agent seats
QA-test a running web app with verifier agents
layered review of a pull request
visualize a JavaScript project's dependency graph
turn repeated dev tasks into reusable tooling
how_to_run: git clone ~/.cursor/plugins/local/swarmstorm (then Developer: Reload Window in Cursor)
notable: Peer-to-peer file lock negotiation between agents on a shared board, before merge
Build-verify loop where verifier agents test the running product and findings feed the next build
Per-project workbenches: project skills plus live pages on real data
Works across Claude Code, Codex and Cursor with the same skills, using each harness's manifest
caveats: Requires Node 22.5 or later; Cursor allows only one level of agent nesting, so workers cannot launch sub-workers there
Workers need an allow rule added to settings.json for shell commands, and the rule must be rewritten after each update
Codex needs agents.max_depth set to 2 or more; on Cursor Enterprise an admin must enable local plugin imports
Cost can be high: the README notes its own editorial run used fourteen Opus seats
